title: [epic] IMAP server (usenet-ipfs-imap crate)
description:
Add a full IMAP4rev1 server as a new usenet-ipfs-imap crate, sharing the same backing stores as the JMAP mail server (ArticleNumberStore, OverviewStore, UserFlagsStore, IPFS block store).

## Design decisions

**TLS**: Implicit TLS only (IMAPS, port 993). Plaintext connections are not accepted — the listener wraps every TCP connection in TLS before the greeting is sent. STARTTLS is not offered or needed.

**Authentication — required mechanisms**:
- AUTH=PLAIN (RFC 4616): username/password over the already-encrypted channel.
- AUTH=LOGIN: older username/password mechanism; required for broad MUA compatibility.
- AUTH=SCRAM-SHA-256 (RFC 5802): challenge-response; password never leaves the client in plaintext even at the application layer; provides mutual authentication. This is the 'improved' mechanism.
- SASL EXTERNAL (RFC 4422) / client certificate: if the TLS handshake presented a valid client certificate, the certificate identity is used as the credential. Two sub-modes:
  a. Exact cert match: the specific certificate (fingerprint) is pre-registered to a user account.
  b. Issuer trust: any certificate signed by a configured trusted CA/issuer is accepted; the Subject CN or SAN email is mapped to the account. Allows organisations to issue per-user certs from their own CA without registering each cert individually.

**Protocol toolkit**: imap-codec + imap-types + imap-next (duesee/* crates). These handle all parsing, serialisation, LITERAL flow, and IDLE. Do not write a custom parser.

**Core commands required**: CAPABILITY, NOOP, LOGOUT, LOGIN, AUTHENTICATE, SELECT, EXAMINE, LIST, STATUS, APPEND, FETCH, STORE, SEARCH, COPY, EXPUNGE, CLOSE, IDLE (RFC 2177), UID variants of FETCH/STORE/SEARCH/COPY.

**Reuse from existing crates**: TLS config and loading from usenet-ipfs-reader/mail tls modules; UserFlagsStore for \Seen/\Flagged/\Answered/\Deleted/\Draft; ArticleNumberStore for UIDs and mailbox enumeration; OverviewStore for SEARCH and ENVELOPE fetch; IPFS block store for FETCH BODY[].
